import re

def slugify_v1(text):
    """Simple approach - remove all non-alphanumeric except spaces, then join with hyphens"""
    text = text.strip().lower()
    # Replace all non-alphanumeric characters (except letters and spaces) with a space
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9\s]+', ' ', text)
    # Join multiple spaces with hyphens
    return re.sub(r' +', '-', text)

def slugify_v2(text):
    """Better approach - handle trailing leading punctuation specially"""
    text = text.strip().lower()
    
    # First, remove all non-alphanumeric characters (except letters and spaces)
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9\s]+', ' ', text)
    
    # Join multiple spaces with hyphens
    result = re.sub(r' +', '-', text)
    
    # Remove trailing hyphen if the last character is not a letter
    if result and not result[-1].isalpha():
        result = result[:-1]
    
    # Also remove leading hyphen if first char is not a letter
    if result and not result[0].isalpha():
        result = result[1:]
    
    return result

test_cases = [
    ("Hello World", "hello-world"),
    ("  a   b  ", "a-b"),

    ("! Hello World", "-hello-world"),
    ("Hello World!", "hello-world"),
    (".hello.world.", "-hello-world-"),
    ("a-b-c", "a-b-c"),
]

for input_text, expected in test_cases:
    result = slugify_v1(input_text)
    print(f"{input_text!r}: {result!r}, Expected: {expected!r}, Match: {result == expected}")

import re

def slugify(text):
    """
    Fix for the original bug where multiple spaces/punctuation created extra hyphens.
    
    The issue was: ["C++ rocks!"] -> "c---rocks-" (wrong!)
    Should be: "c-rocks"
    
    Solution: Replace consecutive non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen,
    but ensure we don't create hyphens at the start or end of the string.
    """
    text = text.strip().lower()
    
    # Replace any sequence of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen
    # This handles multiple spaces, punctuation, etc.
    result = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text)
    
    # Remove leading and trailing hyphens if they are not part of an alphanumeric word
    # A hyphen is only valid if it's preceded or followed by a letter
    if result and result[-1] == '-':
        result = result[:-1]
    elif result and result[0] == '-':
        result = result[1:]
    
    return result

test_cases = [
    ("Hello World", "hello-world"),
    ("  a   b  ", "a-b"),
    ("C++ rocks!", "c-rocks"),
    ("abc", "abc"),
    ("abcdefghij", "abcde..."),
]

print("Comparing implementations:")
for input_text, expected in test_cases:
    result = slugify(input_text)
    print(f"{input_text!r}: {result!r}, Expected: {expected!r}, Match: {result == expected}")
